newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso closes 1.8 lower at 1,004.00.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso closes 1.8 lower at 1,004.00.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed 1.8 lower at 1,004.00 in the first day of trading since last Friday, when Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo warned that the central bank was prepared to intervene aggressively to halt the currency's recent rise.
Traders attributed the peso's slight move downward to position-squaring by banks and said there was no real demand for dollars in active trading that saw 376 operations for a total of $142 million.
There was also no sign of central bank intervention, the traders said.

Banks and financial markets were closed Monday for the All Saints Day holiday. Ocampo announced Friday that the central bank had agreed to intervene in the interbank market as often as necessary to halt the peso's run-up since early June, when it was trading at 1,074 to the dollar. The stronger currency has prompted calls from exporters for a sharp devaluation to help make Colombian goods more competitive abroad. It has also eroded the value of export earnings.
The peso hit an intraday low of 1,007.95 before moving higher ahead of the close.
Its high for the day was 1,003.00 and traders said key resistance was at the pyschological barrier of 1,000-to-one that it breached briefly in intraday trade last Thursday.
